Detailed method

The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 58% hydration, 2% salt, and 0.9% yeast. That is 290 g water, 10 g salt, and 4.5 g yeast, 804.5 g of dough. The balls fields open at 10 rolls of 80.45 g. Fold a star into each firm round, then bake with steam so the pattern stays sharp. Sesame on top, if you add it, is extra and is not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 290 g water, 10 g salt, and 4.5 g instant yeast, then knead for 8 to 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and firm. At 58% hydration it feels stiff, not soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. With 0.9% yeast it should grow by about half, not double.
  3. Divide Divide the 804.5 g dough into 10 pieces of 80.45 g, the weight in the balls fields. Roll each into a smooth round, cover, and rest 10 minutes.
  4. Fold the star Pat a round flat. Fold five lobes over the center, each one overlapping the last, so they meet in a star. Tuck the last lobe under the first so the pattern holds. If you have a kaiser stamp, press it into the round instead. Either way the top should show five curved sections.
  5. Proof Set the rolls star-side down on a floured cloth so the folds do not open. Cover them for 30 to 45 minutes, until they look puffy. Turn them star-side up before baking.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). For the first minutes, give the oven steam: a pan of hot water on the bottom rack is enough. Bake 14 to 18 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the star is still clear.
  7. Cool Set them on a rack for at least 15 minutes before you split one.
